research_question: Can a neural architecture trained natively as low-fan-in Q.ANT Fourier blocks retain useful FashionMNIST accuracy while reducing reference-to-Q.ANT numerical discrepancy?
observations: Exp022 reduced mean logit MAE by about 86 percent when the same g4 model was evaluated as 16 smaller Q.ANT calls instead of one monolithic call.
Exp022 did not change the learned architecture; it only changed evaluation grouping.
A hierarchical model can make low fan-in an architectural property rather than an evaluation-time decomposition.
hypothesis: A two-stage hierarchical QFourier model built from low-fan-in blocks will show substantially lower reference-to-Q.ANT disagreement than a monolithic g4 classifier while retaining competitive FashionMNIST accuracy at a comparable parameter scale.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if the hierarchical model fails to reduce logit error and prediction disagreements, or if its reference accuracy drops by more than 2 percentage points relative to the monolithic g4 baseline.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
The hierarchical model has a different function class and fewer parameters than the monolithic baseline, so accuracy and numerical agreement must be considered jointly.
FashionMNIST is still a small benchmark and does not establish generality.
